entries.root_cause: uvicorn.access has propagate=False and its own StreamHandler bound to uvicorn's AccessFormatter, so its records never reach the root JSON handler installed by configure_logging(). Same process, same stderr sink, same request.

entries.caveat: Passes on every element AC4 names explicitly. Shares QA-VM-003's root cause: the uvicorn access line emitted during the same request carries no request_id. AC4 omits the quantified '100% parse as JSON' clause that AC3 states, so the literal text is met.

entries.caveat: Redaction is opt-in: RedactionFilter only scrubs values a caller explicitly marks via redact_values(). It does not scrub record.exc_info/exc_text -- demonstrated leak of a marked value through a rendered traceback. No group A endpoint accepts PII, so this is latent, not live.
interactions: direct execution of RedactionFilter with redact_values() over a message and a rendered exception

entries.caveat: The guard is materially weaker than the AC text. _count_float_usages counts only float() calls and float literals; it reports 0 for true division, math.*, power and round(a/b), all of which yield Python floats. The Money type itself is genuinely float-safe at runtime.
interactions: replayed the AST counter over 8 synthetic float-arithmetic cases

measured.runtime_float_rejection: InvalidMoneyAmountError on float, bool, and float scalar multiply

entries.caveat: Same guard weakness on the frontend. The forbidden-pattern list misses .toNumber(), .valueOf(), Math.*, unary-plus coercion and bare float-literal arithmetic. Note \bNumber\s*\( does not match .toNumber( because there is no word boundary between 'o' and 'N'.
interactions: replayed the 5 forbidden regexes over 8 synthetic float cases in node
